tools.name: studio_project
tools.description: Read the open video project, its media/tracks/clips/concept, list saved projects, save the current project, or inspect undo history. project.get {ifProjectId?,ifRevision?} returns {unchanged:true,id,revision} when both still match. project.save {} saves the project where it already lives; it takes no path. project.notice {} returns a startup notice such as a recovered project. Projects cannot be created, opened, switched or deleted from here. All times are seconds. Read project.get before editing.

tools.name: studio_edit
tools.description: Apply real edits to Studio and its visible timeline. Methods: edit.add {mediaId,trackId,start,duration,text}; edit.update {id,patch,expectedRevision}; edit.split {id,time:absolute,expectedRevision?}; edit.trim {id,start?:absolute,end?:absolute,expectedRevision?} (retain absolute timeline range, omit unchanged boundary, minimum one frame, source-bounded extension allowed); edit.delete {ids,ripple}; edit.duplicate {ids}; edit.group/ungroup {ids}; color.importLut {id,path,expectedRevision}; edit.track {id,patch} or {kind,name?,clipIds?} (create a compatible layer and optionally move clips, one undo); edit.trackDelete {id} (removes the track and its clips, one undo, locked tracks are refused); edit.trackMove {id,index}; edit.marker {time,label}; edit.markerUpdate {id,time?,label?}; edit.markerDelete {id}; edit.paste {clips,at,expectedRevision?} (inserts copies of the given clip objects with new ids so the earliest starts at at, one undo); edit.batch {commands:[{method,params}],expectedRevision} (atomic, one undo); history.undo/redo; project.update {patch}; media.import {paths}; media.relink {id,path,expectedRevision?} (point media flagged missing:true at a moved file, one undo); media.remove {id}; media.reprobe {ids,expectedRevision} (refresh metadata and repair album-art MP3 clips without changing timing, one undo); media.importAndAdd {paths,start?,trackId?,expectedRevision?}; captions.import/export {path} (export writes only a new file inside the Studio exports folder or the user Movies, Documents, Desktop, Downloads or Music folders). Built-in filter ids are none, cinematic, warm, cool, mono, vintage. Use exact IDs from project.get. Never report unsupported edits as completed.

tools.name: studio_export
tools.description: Render actual output or inspect a composited preview frame. export.start {path,width?,height?,fps?,format?,start?,end?} returns job id; path must be a new file inside the Studio exports folder or the user Movies, Documents, Desktop, Downloads or Music folders, existing files are never overwritten (FILE_EXISTS). export.status {id} reports progress and success/failure. export.cancel {id}. preview.frame {time,width?} returns the rendered frame as an image.

tools.name: studio_memory
tools.description: Use ByoriDB creative memory. memory.search {text?,limit?} recalls concepts, edits and feedback across projects. memory.record {body,kind?,clipId?} records intent or feedback for the current project. Distinguish user-confirmed feedback from your own hypothesis; do not invent observations.

tools.name: studio_speech
tools.description: Local speech processing. speech.status lists available voices and Whisper. speech.transcribe {language:ko|en|auto,model:tiny|base|small,translate?:bool} transcribes the current timeline and inserts captions. speech.synthesize {text,voice?,rate?,start?} creates narration and inserts audio. Both return job id; poll speech.job {id}, cancel with speech.cancel {id}. First transcription downloads the model. Changed projects are not overwritten.

tools.name: studio_assets
tools.description: Manage reusable local fonts and filter/effect presets. assets.list {}; fonts.import {path,name?} accepts TTF/OTF; fonts.apply {id,clipId,expectedRevision}; presets.save {clipId,name,kind:filter|effect}; presets.import/export {path,id?} uses Studio JSON (export writes only a new file in the allowed output folders); presets.apply {id,clipId,expectedRevision}. fonts.remove/presets.remove {id} remove catalog entries. Applying uses the same validated undoable editor commands. Never describe arbitrary executable plugins as supported.
